hint.text:
If the direct speech is not at the start of the sentence, a comma goes after the introductory clause and before the first speech mark.

If the direct speech is at the start of the sentence, the comma goes before the final speech mark.

If the direct speech ends with another kind of punctuation, such as a question mark or an exclamation mark, no comma is needed at the end.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that correctly uses punctuation for the direct speech.
